summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (Jan 2.28/4610)

data.translation: Unless he is standing and sitting at the command, he gets up and sits down at the command of that great man of his. He is always tormented. <...>

rationale: First Detransitive Part. Pass. example; masculine state predicate with yo and domination context. English is supplied project machine translation.

data.translation: So the king gave his orders. They tortured him. They picked out his eyes. They smashed his skull, etc. Nevertheless, he did not commit blasphemy.

rationale: Fill thin active Preterit 1 with plural torturers and a recoverable victim.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 86/32)

data.turoyo: Kətli mede, kqawrile, kməfqile saġ, kmoḥalle, kqəṭlile, koṯən matralle w mʕaḏbile w mbašlile bi nuro — i ḥeṭo.
data.translation: Ich weiss etwas, das begräbt man und zieht es gesund wieder heraus: dann schlägt man es und tötet es; man kommt und benetzt es, drückt es und kocht es am Feuer. (Der Weizen).

data.turoyo: Məlla: "Ya abre d ʕammi! Kalux kul yawmo komamtat ṣaydo ġalabe w ono w hat b tane na. L mə gəmʕaḏbat ruḥux?""
data.translation: Sie sprach: Vetter! Du bringst doch jeden Tag viel Wildbret ins Haus und wir beiden sind doch ganz allein! Was willst du dich abquälen?

rationale: Bring ordinary active Infectum 1 coverage to five with an explicit reflexive ruḥux, distinct from Detransitive morphology.

rationale: Bring Detransitive Preterit coverage to five with first-person plural completed effort.

summary: The broad inherited II 1 gloss already includes quälen, bemühen, belästigen and the Detransitive leiden. Keep this combined sense structure and its numbering; reader D1 is mapped to 1 with detransitive=true.

PrS 5/13 and 73/394 show Detransitive effort or exertion, without an external torturer. Talay 1/139 is suffering with a companion, and 1/142 ongoing afflicted suffering. The Detransitive does not have one uniform function.
52/107 has the active Infectum gəmʕaḏbat plus the explicit reflexive object ruḥux. Do not move it into the Detransitive solely because the German says sich abquälen.

PrS 86/32 is a riddle with coordinated burying, killing, wetting, tormenting/pressing and cooking of wheat. Its ‘kneading’ interpretation is plausible in context but does not prove a craft-language technical sense; record a personification extension only.

Lookup of ʕzb confirms the same Arabic etymon and a single LB 171 Infectum example with z where Talay 1/171 has ḏ. Preserve both attested spellings and cross-references; cross-index that occurrence rather than adding a duplicate or replacing z with ḏ.

36/106 and 36/112, 44/51 and 44/55, and Talay 1/118,121,139,142 are already quoted in this entry under their Ritter/LB references. Do not add them again. Nonphysical harassment (94/509) stays within belästigen.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. English accompanying the added examples is the supplied project machine translation, copied and cut without retranslation; lexical decisions rest on the Turoyo.
The inherited combined sense already includes active torment/harassment and Detransitive suffering. D1 is a reader convenience, not an additional glossary label.
mʕaḏbo yo is masculine in this context and supports a Part. Pass. state predicate; mʕaḏbi in the labour account is plural finite/dependent suffering, kept in Detransitive Preterit.
The new active Infectum-wa form -wolən is provisionally accepted from the unexpressed third-person agent morphology and plural patient. No hypothetical Preterit-wa suffix is inserted.
Jan does not resolve the round-1 question of consolidating the ʕzb spelling variant. Source ḏ is retained.
Does mʕaḏb- mean kneading in ordinary craft speech, independently of the personifying wheat riddle PrS 86/32? No technical sense is published without that evidence.
Talay 1/120 prints mʕaḏbutəlle in a first-person context beside -lli. Verify the ending against the source; it has not been silently corrected.
Should the variant ʕzb be cross-indexed or consolidated with ʕḏb? The shared LB 171 passage confirms overlap but does not license normalizing the source spellings.
Jan 2.4/831: confirm mʕaḏab-wo-lən as Infectum-wa and rule out a contracted Preterit-wa agent plus object sequence.
Jan 2.4/670: segment mʕaḏeballox and identify agent person/number; machine first-person English does not resolve the ending.
Jan 2.28/4610: confirm masculine mʕaḏbo yo as Part. Pass. rather than a lexical adjective; the predicate clearly describes ongoing torment.
In a wheat riddle, processing grain is personified as torment alongside burial and killing. This does not establish an ordinary technical verb ‘knead’.
Military labour and subordination under a powerful man instantiate suffering with no overt torturer phrase; no new Detransitive sense numbering is needed.
